label: Copy-phase update gate: deterministic on short (L=3/4) sequences, sparse elsewhere
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L); it never fires on original-input steps or the delimiter, and never on recall_idx 0. Its most reliable and strongest firing is on short sequences: for L=3 it fires on both copy steps (recall_idx 1 and 2) with about 99.5% precision, and the top activations are on the final copy step of L=3 sequences (e.g. c 3 t <DEL> c [3]). For L=4 it fires reliably at t=6 (recall_idx 2, the second-to-last output; about 80% precision). Together these give dev precision 0.85 but only 46% of activation mass. On longer sequences (L>=5) it fires at weaker magnitude in runs of 1-2 consecutive copy steps, mostly at recall_idx>=2 and not in the first copy steps. Where in the copy phase these runs land varies (concentrated near absolute t=11-13 and 17), and they are only weakly tied to the input token: p, 3, u, x, 2, g are about 2-3.4x more likely than average. I could not find a clean rule for the long-sequence firings, so the predicate covers only the short-sequence part. Calling every copy step active gives recall 1.0 but precision 0.12.
